message.content:
The supplied structure is reported in an orthorhombic, body-centered Imma setting: the lattice is defined by [[cell.a]], [[cell.b]], and [[cell.c]], with all interaxial angles constrained to [[cell.alpha]], [[cell.beta]], and [[cell.gamma]]. Its public symmetry designation is [[space_group.number]], with Hall symbol [[space_group.hall]], and the input description contains [[input.atom_count]] atoms distributed as [[composition.Li]], [[composition.Ni]], [[composition.O]], and [[composition.V]]. Because the standard-from-input frame uses [[frame.matrix]] together with [[frame.origin_shift]], the input cell and the standard crystallographic frame coincide, with no reorientation or origin displacement; fractional values are presented to [[round_digits]].

The independent Wyckoff content separates the metals onto fixed special positions and leaves only oxygen with adjustable fractional coordinates. Lithium occupies two distinct fixed orbits, [[orbit.o000.id]] as [[orbit.o000.element]] on [[orbit.o000.wyckoff]] and [[orbit.o001.id]] as [[orbit.o001.element]] on [[orbit.o001.wyckoff]]; both have no free positional parameters in the Imma expansion. Vanadium is placed on [[orbit.o002.id]] as [[orbit.o002.element]] at [[orbit.o002.wyckoff]], while nickel occupies [[orbit.o003.id]] as [[orbit.o003.element]] at [[orbit.o003.wyckoff]], again on fixed sites whose symmetry images are generated entirely by the body-centered orthorhombic operations.

Oxygen is described by two independent eightfold-type orbits in words rather than by a single rigid oxygen backbone. The first, [[orbit.o004.id]], is [[orbit.o004.element]] on [[orbit.o004.wyckoff]], with free coordinates [[orbit.o004.parameters]] corresponding to a member varying along x and z while held at the fixed quarter-level in y. The second, [[orbit.o005.id]], is [[orbit.o005.element]] on [[orbit.o005.wyckoff]], with free coordinates [[orbit.o005.parameters]] corresponding to variation in y and z on the fixed zero x-plane. No precision-correction entries are supplied, so there are no additional measured displacements from the idealized fixed-metal backbone beyond the stated free oxygen parameters; the small non-round values retained in those oxygen parameters should therefore be read as reported coordinate precision, not as evidence of an extra symmetry-lowering distortion.
